findings.heading: Transmission matrix / 感染伝播マトリックス
findings.proposition: The Japanese prose instructs the reader to load the linelist with `import()` from the rio package, but the code chunk immediately below it (jp lines 51-57) loads the linelist with `appliedepidata::get_data(name = "linelist_cleaned_rds")`, which is what the English prose describes.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader follows the prose, writes an `rio::import()` call against a manually downloaded file path, and diverges from the chunk the rest of the chapter runs on. If the download link fails or the file is saved elsewhere, `linelist` is never created and every later chunk in the chapter errors.

findings.heading: Transmission matrix / 感染伝播マトリックス
findings.proposition: The Japanese text states that the cleaned linelist can be downloaded as an .rds file from the URL https://github.com/appliedepi/epirhandbook/raw/main/data/case_linelists/linelist_cleaned.rds; the English gives no download URL and instead says to load the data directly with `appliedepidata::get_data()`.
findings.reader_consequence: The Japanese reader is sent to a hard-coded repository path that the English edition no longer relies on. If that path moves or is removed, the reader has no working route to the data, while the English reader does.

findings.heading: Transmission matrix / 感染伝播マトリックス
findings.proposition: The Japanese text adds that `import()` handles many file formats such as .xlsx, .rds and .csv, and cross-references the Import and export chapter (#importing); the English sentence contains neither claim and instead cross-references the Download handbook and data page.
findings.reader_consequence: The Japanese reader is pointed at a different chapter for data access than the English reader, and takes away a claim about rio file-format support that this chapter never demonstrates, reinforcing the wrong loading route.

findings.heading: Transmission matrix / 感染伝播マトリックス
findings.proposition: The English explains WHY the Contact tracing page's dataset is simpler: the ages of cases and of their sources are already neatly aligned in the same row of the data frame. The Japanese keeps only the parenthetical "more simple" and drops the explanation.
findings.reader_consequence: The Japanese reader cannot tell what makes the alternative dataset simpler, so cannot judge whether their own data resembles it and whether they can skip the long data-manipulation route this chapter takes.
